name: runTableAggregation
description:
Runs an aggregate function on a table field. Corresponds to GET /tables/{tableId}/runAggregation. Requires `tables:read` scope. [READ-ONLY]

The response includes `matchingRecords`, `evaluatedRecords` and `truncated`; when `truncated` is true only part of the data was aggregated. Without sortOptions the NEWEST records (by _createdAt) are kept when limit is below the number of matching records. Timestamp fields support min, max, count and uniqueValues (min/max/count are computed from the records endpoint because the API itself only allows uniqueValues on timestamps).

function.description: Aggregate function. Numeric fields: all. Text: count, mode, uniqueValues. Boolean: count, mode. Timestamp: min, max, count, uniqueValues. Image, file and linked-record fields cannot be aggregated. uniqueValues returns at most 1000 values.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to evaluate (1-100000, default 100000). Records beyond the limit are dropped, newest kept unless sortOptions say otherwise.

sortOptions.description: Which records to keep when there are more than `limit`, in priority order. Default: [{"sortBy":"_createdAt","sortDir":"desc"}] (newest first). Note: the API currently returns 500 for _sequenceNumber here; use _createdAt.

field.description: Column name (from getTable .columns[].name), or a built-in such as _createdAt.

arg.description: Value to compare to. Omit for 'blank' and 'notBlank'. Numbers and booleans may be sent as text; they are converted to the column's type. For isIn/notIsIn give a comma list ("A,B") or a JSON array. Interval values are in seconds. For timestamps use an ISO 8601 string.
